title: Pin reproducible perf-lab environment (driver/CUDA + container digest) and document setup
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Why
Benchmark runs in perf-lab have been too noisy to confidently attribute FP8/INT8 deltas to kernel/scheduler changes. We’ve seen variance driven by driver/CUDA drift, unpinned containers, inconsistent GPU clock settings, and node contention.

Goal
Create a reproducible, pinned perf-lab environment (GPU driver + CUDA userspace + container image digest + runtime build flags), and document the setup so anyone can rerun the FP8/INT8 benchmark matrix and get comparable results.

Scope
- Pin NVIDIA driver version(s) for perf-lab nodes used by benchmark matrix (A100, H100, H200, L40S).
- Pin CUDA userspace in the benchmark container (and publish the container digest used for official runs).
- Ensure GPU clock/power settings are explicitly set (or explicitly recorded if we cannot enforce).
- Record environment metadata into benchmark result artifacts (nvidia-smi, driver, CUDA runtime, container digest, git SHAs).
- Document: how to provision/verify a node; how to run the pinned container; how to validate environment before a run.

Non-goals
- Solving general cluster contention (tracked in INT-842).
- Migrating to MI300X / ROCm support.

Proposed pinned baseline (initial)
- Host OS: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
- NVIDIA driver: 550.54.15 (fleet-standard for H100/H200 in perf-lab)
- CUDA userspace in container: CUDA 12.4.1
- NCCL: 2.21.x (as provided by base image)
- Container base: nvidia/cuda:12.4.1-cudnn9-runtime-ubuntu22.04

Deliverables
1) "perf-lab" runtime build target + container metadata stamping (git SHA + compiler flags).
2) A canonical container tag + immutable digest used for the sprint benchmark matrix.
3) Pre-run validation script that blocks if the node/container doesn’t match the pinned baseline (or writes a prominent warning + tags results as non-canonical).
4) Confluence runbook section: “Perf-lab Environment (Pinned)” + troubleshooting.

Links
- Runtime: PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/10626 (perf-lab build target + reproducible metadata stamping)
- Benchmark harness: PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmark-lab/pull/412 (config schema supports explicit runtime/container/GPU pins)
- Canary: PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-canary/pull/188 (nightly quant-perf job depends on pinned env)

Acceptance criteria
- We can point to a single container digest for “official” FP8/INT8 sprint runs.
- Running the same benchmark scenario twice on the same GPU SKU in perf-lab yields stable results (target: <2% run-to-run variance on tokens/sec and <3% on TTFT/TPOT p95 after warmup, absent code changes).
- Every uploaded benchmark artifact includes: host driver version, CUDA runtime version, container digest, GPU clocks (or ‘default’), and runtime commit SHA.
- Runbook updated with step-by-step instructions + validation checklist.
acceptance_criteria: Publish canonical benchmark container tag and immutable digest; use it for the sprint matrix runs.
Perf-lab nodes used for official runs are pinned to a documented NVIDIA driver version (or explicitly declared exceptions).
Add preflight validation that records driver/CUDA/container/git SHA to artifacts and warns or blocks when out of spec.
Runbook includes: node verification commands, how to launch pinned container, and how to interpret preflight output.
Variance targets met on a representative scenario (streaming chat + non-streaming batch) on at least H100 and A100.
comments: 2025-10-02 (Sean Gallagher): Root cause recap from noisy runs: we had 3 separate sources of drift (node driver mismatch, container tag moved, and application clocks not consistently set). Proposing we treat env pinning as a first-class input in benchmark-lab configs and reject runs missing immutable digests.

2025-10-03 (Rina Kobayashi): +1. I can wire the config schema to require runtime_commit + container_digest for matrix generator. Need SRE to confirm which driver versions are safe across H100/H200/L40S without destabilizing the rest of the lab.

2025-10-04 (Allison Grant): For dashboards, please emit tags: driver_version, cuda_runtime, container_digest, and a boolean canonical_env=true/false. Otherwise we’ll end up comparing apples/oranges in panels.

2025-10-06 (Connor O'Brien): Release note risk: anything that changes build flags / toolchain needs to be tracked. Please stamp compiler flags + git SHA into the runtime binary and export via the benchmark structured logs so we can audit what ran.

2025-10-07 (Sean Gallagher): Implemented node preflight: checks nvidia-smi driver, persistence mode, and prints current clocks. We can’t enforce app clocks on all SKUs due to permissions on shared nodes; marking runs as canonical_env=false unless clocks match the pinned profile OR the node is on the isolated queue (INT-842).

2025-10-10 (Noah Patel): Ran A/B sanity: two consecutive runs on H100 with pinned digest show ~1.1% variance tokens/sec decode-heavy and ~2.4% variance TTFT p95 on streaming scenario after discarding first warmup run. Looks within target.
updates: 2025-10-04: Drafted pinned baseline proposal (Ubuntu 22.04 + driver 550.54.15 + CUDA 12.4.1 userspace). Coordinated with infra on feasibility for H200 bring-up.
2025-10-07: Landed runtime perf-lab build target w/ metadata stamping; benchmark-lab schema supports explicit pins.
2025-10-09: Added preflight validation + artifact metadata fields; updated runbook section with commands/checklist.

implementation_notes:
Pinned environment approach
- Treat the benchmark container digest as the source of truth for CUDA userspace + NCCL + auxiliary libs.
- Treat node driver as a controlled input (documented and verified via preflight).
- Stamp runtime build metadata (git SHA, compiler flags, build mode) into the binary and export through structured perf logs.

Preflight checklist (automated)
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version,pstate,clocks.sm,clocks.mem,power.limit --format=csv
- nvcc --version (container) and libcudart.so version
- container digest (from runtime env var injected at launch) and image tag
- runtime commit SHA + build flags (from runtime self-report)
- node name + perf-lab queue label (isolated vs shared)

Canonical env rules
- canonical_env=true only if: driver_version matches pinned list AND container_digest matches the configured digest AND runtime_commit matches configured SHA. Otherwise canonical_env=false and results are excluded from dashboards by default.

Docs
- Added/updated runbook section: “Running benchmarks in perf-lab -> Environment (Pinned)”, including troubleshooting for driver mismatch and common sources of variance (power cap changes, background processes, MIG).
risk_and_mitigations:
Risks
- Driver pinning may diverge across GPU SKUs (H200 vs L40S) and prevent a single universal baseline.
- Shared-node permissions may prevent enforcing application clocks.
- Container digest pinning increases friction for quick iteration.

Mitigations
- Maintain a small allowlist of pinned drivers per SKU and encode in preflight; keep canonical_env semantics consistent.
- Use isolated perf-lab queue (INT-842) for official runs; shared queue only for exploratory profiling.
- Provide an explicit “dev” container tag, but require digest pinning for any run uploaded to the official results bucket/dashboards.
